claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement — not the rounded trip_record copy — and the trace records 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km: an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass, the 0.8 km absolute test and the 20% proportional test.

The trace is unbroken and is NOT impaired for policy purposes. It carries 229 fixes at a 10 s sample interval with 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) (gap over 90 s), (b) (jump over 500 m) or (c) (sustained interval over 30 s) is engaged. No independent corroboration is required, and the rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged on the trace alone.

Trip identity is consistent across the pool, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied: trip_id TRP-00115 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and the timing lines up — accepted 21:07:22, first fix 21:10:00, started_at 21:10:00, ended 21:48:00, charged 21:48:22.

No rider-requested-detour exoneration is available to the driver. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction FROM THE RIDER recorded in the chat_log, naming a place or road specifically enough to act on. The entire log is two messages: the driver's own announcement, 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE', and the rider's one-word 'ok'. The rider directed nothing, named no road, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the clause is unavailable and the 5.78 km excess stands unexcused.

The road-closure route also fails. The only traffic_advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00115-01, is MISSING: weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload. The driver's 'CTE northbound was heavy' is therefore backed by no advisory naming a road, no validity window and no shortest-lawful-alternative distance, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and exonerates nothing. I cite the absence deliberately — a MISSING artifact keeps its id and its absence is itself citable.

The fare model caps the remedy: this is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 fixed at booking, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines cannot be re-computed, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance or time refund is available to this rider however large the excess. I do not ask the tribunal to refund the 5.78 km of extra driving as distance — that money was never the rider's loss.

What the rider IS owed is arithmetic under POL-RD-11(a): the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. charged_total is 39.00; the quote is 34.50; the only properly chargeable pass-through is the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) gantry at 2.50, which the optimal route crosses and which the driven trace passes within 44.5 m of. 39.00 less 34.50 less 2.50 leaves 2.00, refunded in full.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line at 2.00 is a phantom gantry and a billing-integrity failure. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing; the nearest fix in the whole 229-point trace is 5419.29 m from that gantry — the first fix of the trip, before the vehicle had left Marina Bay — and the fare record itself flags the line on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(4) it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity referral.

The rider's own profile does not raise the corroboration bar. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the 4-or-more-and-1-or-fewer trigger in POL-RD-08, so this claim needs no corroboration beyond the trace even though the excess is under 30%.

claims.text: The rider's headline grievance - 28 km driven against a 22 km optimal - is not refundable on this fare model. EV-FARE-00115 carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 sitting on the base_fare line, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and the detour cost the rider nothing on those lines: POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The remedy the rider actually asks for on distance does not exist in this policy.

The money arithmetic confirms there is no distance overcharge to refund. total_charged of 39.00 on EV-FARE-00115 is exactly the 34.50 quoted base_fare plus 4.50 of tolls_erp, with distance_fare 0.00, time_fare 0.00, platform_fee 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and distance_charged_km null. Every dollar above the quote is a pass-through line, not distance and not time.

Of the two ERP lines, only one is even arguably chargeable, and it is chargeable. The 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line lies on the optimal route - optimal_route_source names the Defu Flyover gantry as the single gantry the optimal route crosses - and the trace passes within 44.5 m of that gantry at 21:32:40, far inside the 250 m crossing test POL-RD-09 sets. That line stands and is not refundable.

The one genuinely live item is the 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line the trace never approaches, its nearest fix being 5,419 m away. That is a ledger error: under POL-RD-09(4) it is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity referral. It is not a driver sanction. The driver's statement of record that he never went near an AYE gantry matches the trace exactly, and no adverse finding against him follows from the platform's mis-tagging of that gantry.

The deviation the rider can prove is real but immaterial, and immateriality keeps the driver's profile out of the case entirely. Trace-governed excess is 5.78 km at 25.8% on EV-GPS-00115, which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20% but falls far short of the 50% / 8.0 km MATERIAL gate. No POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is therefore triggered and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available on this trip. Nor does the excess feed a refund, because POL-RD-11 closes the distance route on an upfront quote.

Even if the POL-RD-06 check were run it comes back clean. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523, a rate of 0.19% - well under the 5% limb - and 1 is far under the 3-flag limb, so no pattern is ESTABLISHED. Those two fields are the only profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits for this test, so the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter of 1 and the 4.83 rating carry no weight at all and cannot ground any finding.

The driver's conduct was transparent, not covert. At 21:14:10 he messaged the rider 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE'; the rider read that message and replied 'ok' at 21:14:50, and no message from either side asks for any other route or any waypoint. Under POL-RD-11 the questions that survive an upfront quote are the pass-through lines and the driver's conduct, and on conduct the record shows announcement and assent rather than a hidden detour.

No traffic advisory covers this window, and the driver does not pretend otherwise: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING artifact carrying weight 0.0 on issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its issue detail records that no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE between 21:06 and 21:48 on 8 August 2026. The driver therefore does not invoke POL-RD-03 and does not ask the tribunal to lean on his own 'heavy traffic' explanation. He does not need that exoneration, because POL-RD-11 denies the rider a distance refund whether the excess is excused or not.

Pulling the threads together: of the 6.00 contested, the distance element is not refundable at all under POL-RD-11, and the only refundable item is the 2.00 unmatched AYE gantry under POL-RD-09(4). To that extent and no further is the rider's claim supported, and that is where POL-GEN-03 draws the line between the present state standing and a partial return of the contested sum.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, on DSP-00115.

What is not in dispute. The trace EV-GPS-00115 is unbroken: 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). The measured deviation is therefore established on the trip's own evidence. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record copy: 28.18 km driven against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (0.8 km and 20%). Trip identity is consistent across EV-TRIP-00115, EV-GPS-00115 and EV-FARE-00115 (all TRP-00115; timings 21:07-21:48 line up), so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged.

Why the distance element is not refundable. EV-FARE-00115 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 carried on the base_fare line, distance_fare 0.00, time_fare 0.00 and distance_charged_km null. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so the detour cost the rider nothing on those lines; POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The rider's claim that the extra 5.78 km should be repaid therefore fails, and the driver is right that the $6.00 cannot be recovered as distance.

What is payable. The 39.00 charged is the 34.50 quote plus 4.50 of ERP. The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line at 2.50 is properly chargeable: it lies on the optimal route (optimal_route_source names the Defu Flyover gantry as the one gantry the optimal route crosses) and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it at 21:32:40, inside the 250 m crossing test POL-RD-09 sets. That line stands. The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line at 2.00 is a phantom: the closest fix in the whole trace is 5,419 m away, and the fare record itself flags the line on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own statement that he never went near an AYE gantry matches the trace exactly; the mis-tagging is the platform's billing error and no adverse conduct finding follows from it against the driver.

Exculpation and conduct. The driver's heavy-traffic explanation is not relied on and carries no weight: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory (weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and exonerates nothing (POL-RD-08). The rider's one-word 'ok' to the driver's 21:14:10 announcement is an acknowledgement, not a rider instruction under POL-RD-04 - it names no place or road and waypoint_hint is null on both messages - but that is moot here because POL-RD-11 closes the distance-refund route regardless of exculpation. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL (it does not exceed 50% or 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is triggered; had it been run, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 (0.19%) establishes no pattern. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter and the driver's 4.83 rating are context-only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing.

Result. Of the $6.00 contested, $2.00 is refunded - the unmatched AYE gantry. The 34.50 quote and the 2.50 KPE gantry stand. All artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-FARE-00115 and EV-GPS-00115) sit at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.95. A billing-integrity referral is recorded for the phantom line; it does not disturb or delay the money.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) ERP line on EV-FARE-00115 is an unmatched gantry the driven trace never approaches (closest fix 5,419 m, index 0 at 21:10:00, before the vehicle left Marina Bay), refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this was an upfront-quoted trip, so the money question is narrower than the raw distance figures suggest.

To the rider: you are right that the route was longer than booked. EV-GPS-00115 governs the distance under POL-RD-01 (the trip_record copy is rounded and may not be cited for the threshold test) and gives 28.18 km against a 22.4 km optimal — an excess of 5.78 km, 25.8%, which establishes a deviation but falls short of the material gates (50% and 8.0 km). However, because the fare was quoted upfront at 34.50 (EV-FARE-00115, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE), POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time lines at booking and closes the distance-refund route: POL-RD-02 does not run, so no part of the extra 5.78 km is refundable as distance, however large the excess. Your other point is well taken. ruling.explanation:
Both parties have the facts largely right and agree on almost all of them, so this ruling can be short.

What the trace shows. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00115) is intact: 229 fixes at 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07. Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires — on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip-record copy — the trip ran 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km: an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8%. That clears the establishment gate (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. It does not reach the material gate (more than 50% or more than 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available. Even if that check were run it comes back clean — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 523 completed trips in 90 days — and those two fields are the only profile fields POL-GEN-01 allows for that test; the driver's rating and his lifetime deviation counter play no part in this ruling.

Why the extra distance is not refunded. This was an upfront-quoted trip: EV-FARE-00115 carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 on the base-fare line. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so the detour cost the rider nothing on those lines. POL-RD-02 does not run and the distance refund the rider asks for is not available on this fare model, however large the excess. The driver's 'CTE very heavy' explanation is backed by no traffic advisory — EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing; but that makes no difference, because the distance is not refundable either way, and the driver's advocate rightly did not lean on it. Nor does the detour become rider-caused: the chat log shows the driver announcing the diversion and the rider replying 'ok' — assent to the driver's choice, not an instruction from the rider naming a place or road, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04 gives the driver no exoneration and no compensation.

What is refunded. The fare is 34.50 quoted plus 4.50 of ERP. Of the two gantry lines, the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) gantry at 2.50 is properly chargeable: the optimal route crosses it and the driven trace passes within 44.5 m, inside the 250 m crossing test POL-RD-09 sets. POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged, because the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4).

No driver compensation is due, since the detour was neither rider-requested nor recoverable on a fixed fare. At 21:14:10 he messaged the rider 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE'; the rider read that message and replied 'ok' at 21:14:50, and no message from either side asks for any other route or any waypoint. Under POL-RD-11 the questions that survive an upfront quote are the pass-through lines and the driver's conduct, and on conduct the record shows announcement and assent rather than a hidden detour.

No traffic advisory covers this window, and the driver does not pretend otherwise: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING artifact carrying weight 0.0 on issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its issue detail records that no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE between 21:06 and 21:48 on 8 August 2026. The driver therefore does not invoke POL-RD-03 and does not ask the tribunal to lean on his own 'heavy traffic' explanation. He does not need that exoneration, because POL-RD-11 denies the rider a distance refund whether the excess is excused or not.

Pulling the threads together: of the 6.00 contested, the distance element is not refundable at all under POL-RD-11, and the only refundable item is the 2.00 unmatched AYE gantry under POL-RD-09(4). To that extent and no further is the rider's claim supported, and that is where POL-GEN-03 draws the line between the present state standing and a partial return of the contested sum.
